analysis.title: Treasury rally highlights the opportunity in bonds (UBS House View - Daily US)
key_insights: The S&P 500 fell for a fifth straight session on Wednesday while US Treasuries gained for a third straight session. The 10-year yield fell 4 basis points to 5.06% on lower oil prices, and a USD 16bn 20-year auction drew steady demand.

Fed October minutes showed almost all officials agreed further rate hikes would be needed if the economy evolved as expected. A few said a shift to a more restrictive stance may be required, and two said a move larger than 25 basis points could be warranted if inflation proves more persistent.

UBS expects the Fed to raise rates by 25 basis points next month and again in March 2027, and continue raising into 2027. It sees a higher risk of consecutive hikes after stronger-than-expected inflation data.

Fed funds futures already price more than three additional hikes. UBS argues cumulative tightening and tighter financial conditions limit the need for a prolonged cycle, so Treasury yields have room to fall as markets reassess Fed expectations.

UBS forecasts average US inflation of 2.3% in 2027 versus 3.4% in 2026, citing favorable base effects, lower oil and fading tariff effects. AI-related demand is flagged as an upside inflation risk. San Francisco Fed's Daly, New York Fed's Williams, Boston Fed's Collins and Cleveland Fed's Hammack are cited as backing a more measured pace of tightening.

UBS rates fixed income Attractive and recommends rebalancing toward bonds. Capital losses would offset one year of income only if 2-, 5- and 10-year Treasury yields rose by about 255, 113 and 65 basis points respectively.

Within fixed income UBS sees the best return opportunity in emerging market and high yield bonds. It favors intermediate duration (roughly 2 to 10 year maturities), with shorter-dated bonds in growth-sensitive credit segments.

US managed care shares sold off after CMS proposed tighter oversight of Medicare Advantage risk adjustment. The S&P 500 Managed Health Care Index is down nearly 14% since Monday's close. CMS estimates the package could save almost USD 90bn over 10 years. UBS expects negligible earnings effects over the next two years because similar audit efforts have faced legal challenges and the rule could be delayed by litigation.

UBS views the managed care sell-off as a reassessment of benign policy expectations and positioning, not a change in near-term fundamentals. It sees valuations as reasonable and expects greater volatility from policy headlines as the 2028 election approaches.

Three-month LME copper fell 5.7% to USD 12,471 per tonne on Wednesday, the lowest since April and more than 10% below its peak. Drivers cited are AI growth concerns, Fed tightening weighing on demand and doubts about possible US tariffs on refined copper.

UBS attributes the copper drop to weaker sentiment and rising exchange inventories, not weaker fundamentals. It cites weak mine supply growth, deeply negative treatment charges, strong electrification and grid demand, Shanghai inventories near multi-year lows and a record Yangshan premium over LME spot. It stays constructive and keeps a USD 15,500/mt forecast for mid-2027.

The Australian dollar has nearly erased its 2026 gain against the USD after Australian unemployment rose to 4.9% in October, a five-year high, versus an expected 4.7%. The economy lost 43,500 jobs versus a forecast gain of 25,000. AUDUSD traded below 0.67, its eighth straight daily decline.

The RBA has hiked five times this year to an 18-year high of 4.85%, and its latest hike vote was split 6-3. UBS downgraded the Australian dollar to Unattractive because the housing downturn and rising unemployment raise the risk the RBA is among the first major central banks to cut in 2027.

UBS does not rule out further AUDUSD declines near term but expects USD strength to fade from Q2 2027. It favors the British pound and select emerging market currencies for yield advantage and carry, and advises hedging for investors with significant AUD exposure.
Data to watch on 20 November: Japan October inflation, UK October retail sales and US Michigan Consumer Sentiment for November.

sector_views.rationale: Rated Attractive. Elevated starting yields provide income, and yields have room to fall as Fed expectations are reassessed. Best opportunity in emerging market and high yield bonds, with intermediate duration.
UBS sees negligible earnings impact over two years from the CMS proposal. Valuations are reasonable, but policy headlines will add volatility.
Constructive on copper despite the decline, citing tight mine supply, electrification demand and low Shanghai inventories. Weakness is seen as an opportunity to add exposure.
Downgraded to Unattractive on property downturn and rising unemployment, which raise the chance of RBA rate cuts in 2027.

tension_points.theme: Fed hiking cycle and Treasury yields
tension_points.bull_case: UBS argues additional hikes are already priced in (more than three per futures), a prolonged cycle is unlikely, and inflation should ease to 2.3% in 2027, so yields have room to fall and bonds can rally.
tension_points.bear_case: Fed minutes show almost all officials see more hikes needed, a few want a more restrictive stance, and two said a move above 25 basis points could be warranted if inflation proves persistent. UBS notes a higher risk of consecutive hikes after stronger-than-expected inflation data.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Stronger-than-expected inflation data that leads to consecutive Fed hikes, or yields rising by about 65 basis points at the 10-year, which UBS says would be needed for capital losses to offset a year of income.
